title: Alexander Zverev Begins Reign as ATP World No. 1 at Paris Masters : 선물·상품 : JKN

 Ko Jin-a Reporter 입력 2026.11.04 22:31 [Photo: Wikimedia Commons / Rick Munroe (CC BY-SA 4.0)] PARIS — Alexander Zverev stepped onto the court at the Rolex Paris Masters on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, marking his first competitive appearance since officially ascending to the top of the ATP rankings earlier this week.
 Zverev formally secured the world No. 1 ranking on Monday, Nov. 2, overtaking Jannik Sinner.
 His rise to the summit was confirmed after he defeated Tallon Griekspoor to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open, capping a season highlighted by his first two Grand Slam titles at Roland Garros and the US Open, alongside a runner-up finish at Wimbledon.
 The 29-year-old German became the 30th player to reach the No. 1 spot since the introduction of computerized ATP rankings in 1973. He is also the first German man to hold the position since Boris Becker did so in 1991.
 Reaching the peak at 29 years and six months of age, Zverev is the second-oldest player to claim the top ranking for the first time, behind only Australian John Newcombe, who reached No. 1 at age 30 in 1974.
 Zverev opens his Paris campaign in the second round against Italy's Lorenzo Musetti, who holds a 3-2 advantage in their tour-level head-to-head series. Zverev, however, won their most recent meeting at the Vienna Open in 2025.
 Musetti earned his spot in the second round by defeating Hubert Hurkacz 7-6, 7-6 in the opening round, advancing without facing a single break point throughout the contest.
 Speaking ahead of the second-round encounter, Musetti noted their shared history on the tour. "We always played really great battles, and we both know each other pretty well," Musetti said.
 "We practiced together many times; we faced many times in different situations, on different surfaces and of course a lot of things changed."
 The Paris indoor hard-court tournament has previously been a successful venue for Zverev. He captured the Paris Masters title in 2024 and previously reached the final as runner-up in 2020.
